about: What get-context must know before any plan. These are not a questionnaire: Claude first derives each answer from the context (the request, the conversation, the repo, the user's rules, an existing card) and shows what it derived. Only what it cannot derive becomes a question, using `ask` as a starting point; Claude may also ask other questions the work needs. Each answer is the user's, deduced, or 'not needed'. From the answers Claude draws the conclusions: size, difficulty and pace (pace is never asked). Claude never edits this file.

questions.ask: What do you want to achieve, and how will we know it is done?
questions.why: defines the last stage and how it is verified

questions.ask: Is it personal, for your company, or for a client?
questions.why: pace, who approves, what goes into git

questions.ask: Who decides the timing? Are there deadlines (final and intermediate)?
What already exists: code, decisions, inherited constraints?
questions.why: Discovery, what is not up for discussion

questions.ask: How costly is a mistake (a demo, a product that must last, sensitive data)?
questions.why: how much to discuss, whether a decisions folder is needed

questions.ask: Budget, mandatory technologies, rules (personal data, NDA)?
What do you decide, and what do you leave to Claude?
questions.why: who decides each area of choices

questions.ask: Which parts is the work made of (frontend, backend, app, documents...)?
questions.why: parallel work: independent parts get their contracts discussed first

questions.ask: Where do we keep the decisions: a decisions folder, a single decisions file, or the context card alone?
